first_source.proposed_public_header:
theorem N01Properties.exists_discriminantIncrement_strip_joint_growth
    {D : ReferenceData} {T : MaterialData} {S : PhysicalSpacesData}
    {C : NonlinearGeometryData S} {base loss : ℕ} {ε : ℝ}
    (hN : N01Properties D T S C base loss ε)
    (hS : IsPhysicalSpaces D T S) (hT : IsMaterialData D T)
    (j : ℕ → ℕ)
    (hcell : ∀ m, Ioo (C.left m) (C.right m) ⊆ D.cells (j m))
    (l h : ℕ → ℝ) (hl : ∀ m, C.left m < l m)
    (hh : ∀ m, h m < C.right m) :
    ∃ K : ∀ m, SmoothDirections
      (sectorNeighborhood S base ε ε ×ˢ (Ioo (l m) (h m) ×ˢ univ))
      (fun z : (StateDirections S × ℝ) × PolarPoint =>
        (((originalCoefficients D S C (liftSectorParameter S C z.1)).b z.2 ^ 2 -
            (originalCoefficients D S C (liftSectorParameter S C z.1)).a z.2 *
              (originalCoefficients D S C (liftSectorParameter S C z.1)).c z.2) -
          ((originalCoefficients D S C (C.referenceState, 0)).b z.2 ^ 2 -
            (originalCoefficients D S C (C.referenceState, 0)).a z.2 *
              (originalCoefficients D S C (C.referenceState, 0)).c z.2)) /
          T.H (T.sample (j m)) ^ (3 / 4 : ℝ)),
      ∃ B L : ℕ, base ≤ B ∧ loss ≤ B ∧
        UniformWeightedJointGrowth (pairGrading (sectorGrading S) realGrading)
          (fun m => radialE (D.cellIndex (j m))) K B L

Take the existing original a,b,c strip towers and their unweighted fixed-base bounds; withWeight gives the same W. These are multiplier estimates, so their prior H absorption is legitimate.

For a0,b0 use the genuine original tower precomposed by the continuous linear map F0=(0,fst-spatial): (u,y)↦(0,y). Zero is in U because epsilon>0. The actual lift at zero is (C.referenceState,0). compAffine_apply inserts zero parameter slots and keeps each spatial slot. Apply the original growth at state0 and R=0; enlarge its affine right side from1. This retains the original base/loss.

Build the three actual products in the displayed identity. WeightedJointProducts.mul chooses B,L before every R,n. Align each finite pair by mono, with max only over the finitely many previously selected bases/losses. No derivative-order maximum enters B.
Use actual smoothDirectionsAdd/sub and postLinear(-id). WeightedJointOperations has sub, not an assumed add lemma: b+b0 can be estimated as b-(-b0).

Unfold only public coefficientFamily/mixedDerivative order0/originalCoefficientEntry to identify the normalized increments. H>0 follows from hT and the actual sample; ring/field algebra proves the displayed identity.
Transfer the constructed tower to the literal normalized discriminant with SmoothDirections.congrOn and UniformWeightedJointGrowth.congr. Return that single K before B,L and all derivative orders.
